title: John, the Apostle and the Writers
lead: Four Johns stand behind the writings that bear the name, and how many people they were is an old question. John son of Zebedee was a Galilean fisherman, one of the Twelve and, with Peter and James, of Jesus' inner circle (Matthew 4:21–22; Matthew 17:1). The Fourth Gospel names no author but rests on "the disciple Jesus loved" (John 21:20–24). Papias, early in the second century, names both the apostle John and a "John the Elder", and 2 John and 3 John come from "the elder". The writer of Revelation calls himself John four times, a prophet exiled on Patmos, and never an apostle (Revelation 1:1, 4, 9; Revelation 22:8). Church tradition from Irenaeus on holds that the apostle wrote the Gospel, the letters and Revelation at Ephesus. Many scholars today think of two or three people (Dionysius of Alexandria already doubted that the Gospel and Revelation share a writer), and some (Martin Hengel, Richard Bauckham) identify the Beloved Disciple with John the Elder. No view commands a consensus.
